threads.body: `getContext()` currently reconstructs a new `Context.root().with(Span.wrap(...))` whenever `trace_id`/`span_id`/`trace_flags` are present in Log4j context data, even when the appender is executing on the original application thread with a non-root `Context.current()`. This drops any other context entries (e.g., baggage or custom `ContextKey`s) and changes behavior vs the prior logic that only reconstructed when `Context.current()` was `Context.root()` (async/background thread case).

`ContextCapturingLogRecordProcessor.context` is written from `onEmit(...)` (potentially on a different thread) and read later from the test thread without any happens-before relationship, which can make this test flaky. Mark the field `volatile` (or use an `AtomicReference`) to ensure visibility.

`ContextDataAccessorImpl.forEach(...)` filters out entries whose key equals `OTEL_CONTEXT_DATA_KEY`. Since the lambda already guards on `value instanceof String`, this extra key check is not needed to prevent the carried `Context` object from being turned into attributes, and it makes `captureContextDataAttributes="*"` silently drop a user-supplied string context-data entry named `otel.context`.

threads.body: The new `otel.context` context-data propagation is not currently exercised end-to-end: this test only verifies that the injector adds a `Context` object, but it never asserts that `OpenTelemetryAppender` actually *reads* `OTEL_CONTEXT_DATA_KEY` when `Context.current()` is root (the async/background-thread case). Adding an assertion that a log event with `OTEL_CONTEXT_DATA_KEY` set results in the expected span context would prevent regressions where the appender ignores the carried `Context`.

threads.body: Configuring `OpenTelemetryAppenderContextDataInjector` adds a non-string `otel.context` entry into Log4j context data. If users have layouts that render the entire context/MDC map (e.g., `%X` without a key, or JSON layouts that dump all context data), that key may show up in their log output; it’s worth calling out here so users can exclude it if desired.

threads.body: `rawContextData()` currently just delegates to the underlying `ContextDataInjector`, so `OTEL_CONTEXT_DATA_KEY` is not present on code paths where Log4j reads context data via `rawContextData()` (some event factories use this as a fast path). In those cases async log events won’t carry the full OpenTelemetry `Context`, defeating the purpose of this injector.

threads.body: `injectContextData(...)` always copies/frees a frozen map and adds `OTEL_CONTEXT_DATA_KEY`, even when `Context.current()` is `Context.root()`. In the common case of no active OTel context, this adds avoidable overhead (and can force an allocation if the delegate returns a frozen map) without changing behavior. Consider skipping the injection entirely when the current context is root.

threads.body: `rawContextData()` currently always allocates/copies into a new `StringMap` to add `OTEL_CONTEXT_DATA_KEY`. When `Context.current()` is `Context.root()`, this is unnecessary and defeats the purpose of Log4j's `rawContextData()` fast-path. Returning the delegate's raw context data directly in the root-context case avoids an allocation without changing behavior.
